sections.h2: What can I do if I am facing foreclosure in Margate?
sections.html:
You can sell the house before a court sale takes it, and in Florida that window is often wider than owners expect because foreclosure runs through the courts. The lender files suit in Broward County, wins a final judgment, and only then does the clerk schedule a public sale.

By statute the sale falls no fewer than 20 and no more than 35 days after the judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer gap (s. 45.031). The notice runs for two consecutive weeks. The high bidder leaves 5 percent of the bid, and if no objection comes within 10 days of the certificate of sale, the clerk files the certificate of title and the sale stands.

A faster path exists for some lenders. Under s. 702.10 a lienholder can ask for an order to show cause, with a hearing no sooner than the later of 20 days after service of the order or 45 days after service of the complaint. That path does not apply the same way to owner-occupied homes, and a granted homestead exemption on the latest tax roll is a rebuttable presumption of owner occupancy. Margate owners with a homestead exemption therefore get the ordinary track.

  • Read every court paper and note the response deadline printed on it.
  • Ask your servicer for a payoff figure in writing.
  • Call a Florida foreclosure attorney or legal aid office early.

sections.h2: What happens to extra money if my Margate house sells at a foreclosure auction?
sections.html:
Money left after the lender and liens are paid is surplus, and the owner can claim it through the clerk. The final judgment must carry a surplus notice, and homestead owners are told to check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale.

Claims must be filed before the clerk reports the funds as unclaimed. A voluntary sale on your own terms usually leaves you with more control, because the closing agent pays off the mortgage and you receive what remains at closing.

sections.h2: How much does the deed tax cost when a Margate house sells?
sections.html:
The statute puts the tax on a deed at 70 cents for each $100 of consideration (s. 201.02). Miami-Dade has its own rate; Broward does not, so the 70 cent figure applies to Margate.

Consideration is broader than the price. It includes money paid, any obligation discharged, and any mortgage or encumbrance, whether the buyer assumes it or not. The Department of Revenue says all parties to the document are liable, even where one side agrees to pay, so the sales contract should name the payer. Deeds are taxable whether or not they are recorded, and the clerk collects at recording.

A deed in lieu of foreclosure appears on the Department's taxable list, so handing the keys to the lender through a deed is not free of the tax. A certificate of title after a foreclosure is taxed on the highest and best bid at the sale.

sections.h2: When are Margate property taxes due, and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in November, and the early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent in November to 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1.

An owner who cannot pay in full has options. Homestead owners can apply for a tax deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31 following the assessment year, covering the part of the tax above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Installment prepayment needs an application to the tax collector by May 1 (s. 197.222).

sections.h2: How do tax certificates and tax deeds threaten a Margate owner who stops paying?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes lead to a tax certificate, sold by June 1 to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). The certificate holder cannot contact the owner to demand payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

After those two years, the holder can apply for a tax deed with an application fee of $75 (s. 197.502). The clerk then runs the public auction, and on homestead property the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value on top of the amounts owed. A deadline that looks distant can still be close if the certificate has aged, so ask the Broward tax collector what certificates exist on your parcel before you list.

sections.h2: Which offers suit a Margate owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
A cash purchase makes sense when a court date, a tax certificate or a lien sets the pace. It removes financing and appraisal delay, and the buyer pays for repairs rather than asking you to.

Put the closing date, the payoff and each fee in writing before you sign. The Broward County Property Appraiser can be reached at 954-357-6830 on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm for questions about the exemption on your parcel.

sections.h2: What should I gather before talking to a Margate buyer?
sections.html:
Collect the papers that answer a buyer's first questions, so the offer you receive reflects the real condition of the house and not guesses. Missing papers are the most common cause of a late closing.

  • The mortgage statement with a current payoff figure.
  • Court papers, if a foreclosure suit has been filed, with the case deadlines marked.
  • The latest tax bill and a note of any tax certificate on the parcel.
  • Any homestead exemption notice from the property appraiser.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since all owners must sign.

Florida requires a conveyance of land to be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01), and witnessing may be done by audio-video technology. Ask your closing agent how they handle signing if an owner lives out of state.

Recording charges are set by statute. The clerk charges $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each extra page of a standard instrument, with additional per-page modernization and technology charges (s. 28.24). Put those lines on your net sheet next to the deed tax so the number you expect at closing matches the number you receive.

faqs.q: How soon after a foreclosure judgment is the Margate house sold?
faqs.a: The clerk sets the public sale between 20 and 35 days after judgment unless the plaintiff consents to longer (s. 45.031). The notice is published for two consecutive weeks.

faqs.q: Can I get surplus money after a foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Yes, if any remains after liens and the judgment are paid. File a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed, and homestead owners should check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale.

faqs.q: Is a deed in lieu of foreclosure exempt from deed tax?
faqs.a: No. The Department of Revenue lists a deed in lieu of foreclosure among taxable deeds, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in Broward (s. 201.02).

faqs.q: How does the Florida tax deferral work?
faqs.a: A homestead owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. It defers the part above 5 percent of last year's household income, and for a permanent resident 65 or older the part above 3 percent.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean I lose my house right away?
faqs.a: No. The holder must wait two years after April 1 of the issue year before applying for a tax deed, which carries a $75 application fee (s. 197.502). Ask the Broward tax collector what you would owe to clear the certificate.
